issue_context.title: ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-performance flakes with slow POST/PATCH jobs requests
issue_context.body:
#### Which jobs are flaking:
Two flakes recently:
* https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-performance/1434924831014391808
* https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-performance/1432025635122843648

They fail with error like:
```
:0
[measurement call APIResponsivenessPrometheus - APIResponsivenessPrometheusSimple error: top latency metric: there should be no high-latency requests, but: [got: &{Resource:jobs Subresource: Verb:POST Scope:resource Latency:perc50: 26.798561ms, perc90: 48.23741ms, perc99: 1.063749999s Count:149 SlowCount:2}; expected perc99 <= 1s]]
:0
```

or

```
:0
[measurement call APIResponsivenessPrometheus - APIResponsivenessPrometheusSimple error: top latency metric: there should be no high-latency requests, but: [got: &{Resource:jobs Subresource: Verb:PATCH Scope:resource Latency:perc50: 29.365079ms, perc90: 130ms, perc99: 1.064999999s Count:148 SlowCount:2}; expected perc99 <= 1s]]
:0
```

#### Testgrid link:
https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-release-master-informing#gce-master-scale-performance

/assign
comments:
In https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-performance/1434924831014391808 logs I have found the following slow calls:

```
I0906 19:05:57.328637      12 httplog.go:105] "HTTP" verb="PATCH" URI="/apis/batch/v1/namespaces/test-3cnpmr-40/jobs/small-job-0" latency="1.034064788s" userAgent="clusterloader/v0.0.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/$Format" audit-ID="7ab0bccb-46b4-426c-8fea-ba5a6d63b18c" srcIP="34.134.33.17:39658" apf_pl="exempt" apf_fs="exempt" apf_d="" fl_priorityandfairness="975.523326ms" resp=200
I0906 19:05:57.351657      12 httplog.go:105] "HTTP" verb="PATCH" URI="/apis/batch/v1/namespaces/test-3cnpmr-6/jobs/medium-job-0" latency="1.030253352s" userAgent="clusterloader/v0.0.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/$Format" audit-ID="730817fb-a10c-4e61-92d6-5d85ffd99e6d" srcIP="34.134.33.17:39660" apf_pl="exempt" apf_fs="exempt" apf_d="" fl_priorityandfairness="1.020300711s" resp=200

```
* It's a bug that we use exempt priority level for clusterloader: I created https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/104809
* It's quite worrisome that APF handler takes 1s for exempt request.

I checked a APF code and I think the flow for exempt requests is:
* genericfilters.WithPriorityAndFairness()
   * workEstimate := workEstimator.EstimateWork(r)
   *  fcIfc.Handle()
       * cfgCtlr.startRequest()
          * cfgCtlr.lock.Lock()
          * looks for matching flowschemas in cfgCtrl.flowSchemas
          * returns for exempt
          * for other requests it calculates sha256 for flowDistinguisher and queues request
       * req.Finish
          * updates metrics
          * calls execFn
             * updates headers
             * handler.ServeHTTP which stops the timer for priorityandfairness

For me, the most likely reason for slowness is lock contention on cfgCCtrl.lock. We know that the test is super cpu-intensive in that part and other requests are e.g. calculating sha256 keeping that lock.

A potential improvement would be to change this lock to RWLock or return the lock before starting calculating sha256 (if we believe that this is the most expensive operation there).

/cc @MikeSpreitzer @lavalamp @wojtek-t @tkashem

I think the lock-contention is even worse than what you wrote, as e.g.:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ef754331c453d3b5fdc31edf62da3d90771d5acd/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/flowcontrol/apf_controller.go#L823
is happening under this lock (which is also dispatching requests).

I will take a deeper look later this week, but I think that switching to RWLock might do the job without any invasive changes.

`plState.queues.StartRequest` may trigger the execution of some requests that were waiting, but they are not executed in the same goroutine.

Yes, I think changing that Mutex to a RWMutex would be an easy way to greatly reduce contention.
I agree switching to RWMutex is likely to help a lot, if that's not enough I think with a little work we could e.g. switch to `atomic.Value`s.
(perhaps because that's what my code originally did?  Reviewers thought the retirement dance was too tricky.)

/triage accepted
/priority important-soon
I will work on the fix.

Wow! Thanks a lot for rapid help here! Let's wait for the next test run to see if it helped.
/reopen

Yes, can you please report the filter latency regardless of whether it is bad or good?  I would like to know _how much_ of a difference that PR made.
Sure, will report the latency change in both cases.

I compared 
* (the one where we saw issue) https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-performance/1434924831014391808
* (first with the lock improvements) https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-performance/1435649583614005248

I tried to find requests that:
* use exempt PL (so shouldn't be throttled)
* has fl_priorityandfairness, key which means that priority and fairness filter took more than 100ms

Sample matching request:
```
I0906 20:43:56.160509      12 httplog.go:105] "HTTP" verb="DELETE" URI="/api/v1/namespaces/test-3cnpmr-16/services/small-service-12" latency="466.642329ms" userAgent="clusterloader/v0.0.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/$Format" audit-ID="83b8fcd2-988e-4353-8645-e61d049091b4" srcIP="34.134.33.17:39630" apf_pl="exempt" apf_fs="exempt" apf_d="" fl_priorityandfairness="140.356839ms" resp=200
```

In the old run, I see ~6k such requests, with the locking improvements there are no such requests.
```
$ grep -c -e 'exempt.*fl_priorityandfairness' 1434924831014391808/kube-apiserver.log
5830
$ grep -c -e 'exempt.*fl_priorityandfairness' 1435649583614005248/kube-apiserver.log
0
```

The latency of PATCH jobs seems to improve significantly:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2559168/132639234-3afb76f5-e09f-4a5d-9f65-9f9fbfa6d8f9.png)

So overall it looks great. The only worrisome metric I see is that actual P&F throttling for other requests has grown:

With locking improvements:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2559168/132639639-ff710cbe-5217-4dda-8274-97045ee1d7e4.png)

Old: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2559168/132639650-27daccfc-0a9d-4094-9d75-8c20b6b342fa.png)

E.g. 'node-high' has now throttling latency of ~1.5s in spikes where in the previous test run it was more like ~800ms.

I don't think the lock improvements touched this directly.
I expect that this is either:
* per-test variance (if we rerun the old run again we would see different throttling latencies as well)
* we throttle exempt requests less (as expected) giving less resources to other requests.

Anyway, I don't think this change is meaningful as per-test latency aggregates for PATCH nodes/status and PUT leases (the most common requests in node-high) look ~same as previously:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2559168/132640335-d22b97b9-2bf4-4fc1-be0e-dd69773388eb.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2559168/132640417-f954fa05-72ac-4752-bf1e-5187701edb1b.png)

I think we can close this for now as the issue seems to be resolved.

Thanks a lot @MikeSpreitzer for your help here!
/close

review_comments: is it correct that we're calling UpdateObservations() under a read lock?
Yes.  The locking is carefully documented.  See https://github.com/kubernetes/apiserver/blob/3df972bf11afa6715f44c5a457392ba3ff7b597d/pkg/util/flowcontrol/apf_controller.go#L146-L154
It is not good for that to mean either of these two options, since they are contradictory.

I look at it this way: using "Locked" gives some information.  Not using "Locked" is the complement of that.  Yes, it might be nice to distinguish cases in that complement.  But do you really want to see more stuff added to more func names?

Also, this runs into trouble when implementing an interface.  You do not want an implementation distinction (between "doesn't care about the implementation's lock" and "must not hold the implementation's lock") to appear in the func names in the interface.
I think it would be better to describe the situation like this: "For functions without either suffix, look at the function comment for any locking requirements."
I think that's the obvious conclusion from the existing text, but would be fine with adding that explicit statement.
How would you recommend proceeding, from the current state of the codebase and PRs?

I don't think it's worth changing this since it already merged, I was just (attempting to) note that the comment isn't very helpful, but is written in language that makes it seem like it should be helpful.
